text:
The evidence doesn't establish deforestation, though it does show tree-cover loss.

Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021, roughly 2.2% of the 3,643.5 ha asset. The loss is corroborated: later years were observed, and the JRC 2020 map agrees that 98% of the area was forest.

The territorial context points to planted forest. The MGAP 2021 map puts 68.1 ha of the loss in planted forest (pine species), 0 ha in native forest, and 13.2 ha outside mapped forest. Hansen loss includes any stand replacement, such as harvesting a plantation, so this may be plantation cutting rather than land-use change.

The data does not show the cause, whether land use changed, legality, who was responsible, or any compliance status (including EUDR). A further 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

To assess deforestation, you would need evidence of post-loss land use, such as whether the stand was replanted or converted.
